html:
SMTO-GWT-0024 — The chosen Gateway can't be found or isn't set up correctly

GUID: dfdf2ed3-ff7b-41f3-9a8c-8fc65bc7df4d
Slug: invalid-gateway-target
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't match this request to a Gateway it can use. The Gateway may have been deleted, turned off or renamed, or a saved item still points to an old one.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and make sure the Gateway you want is listed and its Enabled switch is turned on. SMTO can only send work to a Gateway that still exists and is turned on.
  2. In the message box, open the execution target menu, select Refresh targets, then pick that Gateway. This replaces an old or missing choice with a Gateway SMTO can use right now.
  3. If this came from a schedule, open the Schedules page and check which Gateway that schedule uses. If that Gateway was deleted, create the schedule again from a new message. A schedule keeps the Gateway it was created with and won't switch to another one by itself.
  4. If you mentioned a Gateway by name in your message, check the spelling matches its nickname exactly. SMTO matches names in your message against Gateway nicknames.

What success looks like

  • The request starts on the Gateway you picked, and that Gateway shows a check mark in the execution target menu.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Gateways. If an earlier Task was interrupted on the old Gateway, don't rerun it on a different Gateway until you know what it already did.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway target resolution failed: the selected or captured Gateway no longer exists or is disabled, a required node was missing, or a saved resource's Gateway identity, route or connection fields failed validation.

What this means

  • Target resolution could not find the captured Gateway, a request omitted its node, or a saved resource's Gateway identity and transport fields failed validation. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Target resolution could not find the captured Gateway, a request omitted its node, or a saved resource's Gateway identity and transport fields failed validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish a deleted record, missing node and malformed saved route using the producer detail and captured target fields.

How to fix it

  • Read the Technical details to tell which case applies: deleted or disabled Gateway record ("Selected Gateway was not found", "scheduled gateway is no longer available"), missing node ("Node is required"), or malformed saved Gateway identity/route/transport on a database or git working context. Re-select an existing enabled Gateway, or recreate the saved resource against it; do not rewrite the target of a saved run or schedule whose earlier work is unresolved.
  • Correct the target selection or saved route using the intended current Gateway. Preserve the original target of any operation whose outcome is still unresolved.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The requested target resolves to an existing enabled record with consistent node and transport information.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
